To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we isolated the first medaka PCD model, joi, and identified a novel dnai2 gene, and that these two dnai2s are expressed in a redundant and/or distinct manner.

a novel medaka mutant, jaodari, has a left-right (LR)-defective phenotype due to disruption in the outer dyen arms of cilia, and the medaka genome has two dnai2 orthologs, which function either redundantly (in the testis) or distinctly (in the brain and KV).

the joi mutation was found to be caused by genomic insertion, and that the joi gene encodes a protein required for motility of cilia in the Kupffer's vesicles, which are essential for the establishment of left-right asymmetry in the medaka.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the medaka joi mutant.
the characterization of a novel PCD mutant in medaka.
the molecular basis of the motility defects in ciliary and flagellar axonemes, and the role of cilia in medaka LR development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dnai2 is required for the assembly of outer dynein arm in motile ciliogenesis and that the dnai2 gene family plays a redundant and distinct role in motile ciliated tissues.
joi is a medaka PCD model with a severe reduction of the outer dyneins in motile ciliary axonemes.
joi is caused by disruption of dnai2 and that the dnai2 gene is responsible for ciliary motility and KV function in medaka.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the medaka dnai2 genes are essential for the formation and/or maintenance of the outer dyneins, and that dnai2 is required for KV cilia motility and LR specification.
dnai2 is required for motility of cilia in the medaka, but not for LR axis formation.
joi mutants have a severe motility defect in KV cilia, which causes the LR defect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the joi dnai2 mutant is a novel model for PCD, and that there is more than one dnai2 gene that can function in motile ciliogenesis in the medaka.
the joi mutation causes a severe motility defect in KV cilia and results in a LR defect, suggesting that the motility of KV cilia is crucial for the LR axis determination in the medaka embryo.
dnai2 is essential for ciliary motility and that the two dnai2 paralogs have distinct functions.
